attempted_claim: Let E/Q be y^2+y=x^3-x^2-7x+10 (CM by Z[(1+sqrt(-11))/2]), a in {-3,33}, E_a the quadratic twist, and Y=Kum(E x E_a) with affine model u^2=a f(x)f(t). Let A in Br(Y)[3]\Br(Q) be a transcendental 3-torsion class. Is the evaluation map ev_{A,v}:Y(Q_v)->Br(Q_v)[3] constant (hence zero) for every place v != 3 — in particular at v=2 where E has good supersingular reduction and E(Q_2) is not 3-divisible? Equivalently, does Tawfik–Newton Theorem 6.1 extend to the excluded case K=Q(sqrt(-11))?
decisive_failure: No proof or disproof of the target is offered. Partial results (E(Q2)/3=Z/3 for E and both twists, E[3]=C(+)D splitting over Q2 with D=mu_3, reduction to c(1)=c(5)=0) are computationally supported by scripts in work/ but were not elevated to audited claims; the cup-product evaluation requiring F64 plus ramified-cubic 3-descent arithmetic remains open.
